bulletin.morning: The Northern Limit of Monsoon continues to pass through 22°N/60°E, 22°N/65°E, Jamnagar, Udaipur, Ajmer, Jhunjhunu, Hisar, Bhatinda and 32.5°N/70°E. Conditions are favourable for further advance of southwest monsoon into some more parts of North Arabian Sea, Gujarat, remaining parts of Haryana & Punjab, and some more parts of Rajasthan during next 3 days.

met_analysis:
The depression over North-interior Odisha & adjoining south Jharkhand moved northwestwards with a speed of 8 kmph during past 6 hours, and lies centered at 0530 hrs IST of today, the 6th July 2026, over south Jharkhand and adjoining north interior Odisha near latitude 22.4°N and longitude 85.7°E, close to southwest of Chaibasa (Jharkhand) and about 70 km southwest of Jamshedpur (Jharkhand), 110 km of south-southeast Ranchi (Jharkhand), and 170 km east-southeast of Jashpurnagar (Chhattisgarh). It is very likely to move nearly northwestwards across Jharkhand & adjoining north Odisha and North Chhattisgarh during next 24 hours.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now runs from southwest Rajasthan to eastcentral Bay of Bengal across Madhya Pradesh, north Chhattisgarh and the centre of Depression over south Jharkhand and adjoining north interior Odisha and extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The shear zone roughly along latitude 21°N between 3.1 & 7.6 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over eastcentral Arabian sea adjoining Maharashtra coasts at 5.8 km above mean sea level has merged with shear zone.
The offshore trough at mean sea level now runs from south Gujarat to Karnataka coast.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 72°E to the north of Lat. 30°N persists.
